title: Customer Success — Deployment Milestone Sprintboard (CS Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, sprintboard-style implementation tracker to be used by Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering, and the assigned Customer PM during an inference rollout. The emphasis is on clarity: milestone, owner, concrete acceptance criteria, immediate blocker, and next action. Drafted for fast weekly standups and QBR summaries.

How to use (quick):
- Update the milestone status and blocker before the weekly rollout standup (Mon 10am PT).
- If a milestone is blocked for >48 hours, tag the owner and the escalation contact in Slack and add a short note in the 'Escalation log' below.
- For QBR slides, export the 'Completed' rows and the top three risks.

Executive summary (1-2 lines):
- Customer: NovaHealth (example). Primary goal: replace on-prem model endpoint with Redwood Dedicated cluster for 99ms p50 inference for core clinical scoring pipeline.
- Current sprint snapshot: 7 milestones active, 3 behind schedule, 1 critical blocker (network egress policy).

Milestone Sprintboard (ordered by target date):
- M1 | Kickoff & Access Provisioning
  - Owner: Miguel Torres
  - Target: 2025-11-10
  - Status: Complete
  - Acceptance criteria: SSO invited, billing profile created, initial API key issued to customer sandbox, handshake call done.
  - Blocker: none
  - Notes: Customer asked for RBAC mapping template (sent).

- M2 | Network & Security Validation
  - Owner: Lena Wu
  - Target: 2025-11-21
  - Status: Blocked
  - Acceptance criteria: VPC peering (or VPC connector) established, egress rules validated, KMS integration smoke test pass.
  - Blocker: Customer infra team requires explicit outbound egress allowlist for vendor IPs; security change window opens next week.
  - Next action: Lena to schedule security window with customer SRE; escalate if not approved by 2025-11-17.
  - Related tickets: JIRA-1234

- M3 | Model Variant Onboarding & Baseline Eval
  - Owner: Omar Farouk
  - Target: 2025-11-28
  - Status: In progress
  - Acceptance criteria: Customer baseline eval run (10k prompts), perf baseline (p50, p95) documented, quality regression < 2% vs. baseline.
  - Blocker: Intermittent tokenization mismatch with customer preprocessing script.
  - Next action: Omar to push a small normalization shim and re-run sample set.
  - Related artifacts: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/preproc-shims/pull/56

- M4 | Performance Tuning (batching & KV cache)
  - Owner: Priya Nair
  - Target: 2025-12-05
  - Status: At risk
  - Acceptance criteria: Sustained throughput >= 500 rps on Dedicated pool during 8-minute load test; latency p50 < 120ms.
  - Blocker: Need Dedicated pool sizing approved by finance (pending commit).
  - Next action: Priya to confirm committed GPU count for Q1 and adjust autoscale policy.

- M5 | Canary Rollout (10% traffic)
  - Owner: Customer PM (TBD) / CS lead backup: Asha Patel
  - Target: 2025-12-12
  - Status: Planned
  - Acceptance criteria: No more than 0.5% error rate increase vs baseline; rollback plan validated.
  - Blocker: TBD (dependent on M2 and M4)

- M6 | Full Cutover & SLA Handover
  - Owner: Solutions Eng + CS Ops (Priya)
  - Target: 2025-12-20
  - Status: Planned
  - Acceptance criteria: All readiness checks green, playbooks handed over, post-cutover monitoring alerts configured.
  - Blocker: Dependent on Canary success and security sign-off.

- M7 | Post-Launch QBR & Cost Review
  - Owner: Asha Patel
  - Target: 2026-01-15
  - Status: Planned
  - Acceptance criteria: QBR slide deck with usage, cost delta vs forecast, top 3 operational risks, recommended Optimize settings.
  - Notes: This is the deliverable for renewal conversation prep.

Acceptance criteria shorthand (for quick sign-off):
- Functional: feature works end-to-end with sample production traffic.
- Performance: meets agreed latency/throughput SLOs for 3 consecutive runs.
- Security: required controls validated (KMS, network rules, audit logs).
- Operational: runbooks and on-call rotations documented and shared.

Blocker index & triage guidance (CS sprintboard rules):
- P0 Blocker: prevents customer from testing in staging (escalate to Eng SRE + Customer Success Director)
- P1 Blocker: slows progress but workaround exists (Escalate to Solutions Eng lead)
- P2: informational / design question (track, resolve in weekly sync)

Open blockers (current):
- Network egress allowlist (M2) — P0 — owner: Customer infra — notes: awaiting security window; escalate if no window in 48h.
- Tokenization mismatch (M3) — P1 — owner: Omar — notes: validation dataset incomplete; shipping shim by 2025-11-12.
- Dedicated sizing approval (M4) — P1 — owner: Priya — notes: finance requires 3-month forecast; CS to provide projected utilization breakdown.

Escalation log (append-only):
- 2025-11-12 | Escalated network egress to Customer CTO (cc: Redwood SRE). Reason: security window required before we can validate egress rules. Owner: Miguel. Outcome: Waiting for CTO reply.

Runbook & handover checklist (minimal viable):
- Ops runbook created and stored: confluence link (see linked artifacts).
- Pager rota assigned and validated for first two weeks post-cutover.
- SLO dashboard configured with model-level traces and cost per token metric.
- Canary rollback documented (playbook + one-click action).

Weekly update template (paste into standup Slack thread):
- Week of YYYY-MM-DD — Summary: <one sentence>
- Completed this week: <M# names>
- In progress / at risk: <M# names> + short reason
- Blockers (P0/P1): <list with owner + ETA to unblock>
- Next 7 days: <top 3 actions>

QBR-ready pull (for template):
- Completed milestones (dates)
- Current SLA metrics vs target (p50/p95 latency, error rate) — snapshot link to dashboard
- Top 3 remaining risks and mitigation plan
- Renewal recommendation (on track / needs exec review)

Notes / fast wins:
- Bring your own tokenizer: suggested short-term mitigation is to run normalization shim at the Redwood ingress layer until customer retires legacy preprocessing.
- Small perf win: enable kv-cache sticky sessions for inference-heavy flows (can reduce tokens by ~14% in our run).

Action owners (current):
- CS Lead: Asha Patel — overall rollout owner and renewal shepherd.
- Solutions Eng: Miguel Torres — onboarding scaffolding, initial access.
- Security/Networking: Lena Wu — VPC & KMS validations.
- Model Ops: Omar Farouk — baseline evals and model validation.
- CS Ops / Performance: Priya Nair — Dedicated sizing, autoscale policies, cost modeling.

Appendix: Useful snippets and short checklists (for copy/paste)
- Pre-launch checklist (copyable):
  1) API key issued & verified
  2) Network connectivity verified (ping + curl test to health endpoint)
  3) KMS key test encrypt/decrypt success
  4) 3x perf runs within SLOs
  5) Runbooks and rollback steps in Confluence

- 48h escalation message (template):
  Hi <Name>, we are blocked on <component>. This is a blocker for the customer rollout (M2). Impact: prevents staging validation and delays canary. Can you confirm the security window or provide a contact to approve outbound allowlist by EOD?

Draft history and what to polish next:
- 2025-11-02: initial draft created (owner: Asha)
- 2025-11-09: added milestone M3 details after model onboarding run (author: Omar)
- 2026-03-10: trimmed for QBR export and added Weekly update template (editor: Priya)

---
If you want, I can convert the Milestone Sprintboard into a simple sheet layout (CSV) for import to Jira or Google Sheets that includes columns: milestone_id, title, owner, target_date, status, acceptance_criteria, blocker, blocker_severity, next_action, related_tickets. Say the word and I will generate the CSV export next.
